steps.step: Try another adapter and wall socket
steps.expected: The charging light comes on within a minute
steps.resolves_if: It charges with the other adapter: replace the charger

steps.step: BIOS battery reset: unplug, hold power for 30 seconds, then reconnect
Battery health test (powercfg /batteryreport on Windows)
steps.expected: Full-charge capacity close to design capacity
steps.resolves_if: Capacity is under 50% of design: replace the battery

steps.step: Check the charging port for damage or debris
steps.expected: The plug sits firmly without wobbling
steps.resolves_if: A loose or damaged port needs a technician

steps.step: Replace the battery

title: Charger or charging port not working

steps.step: Check the charger's light and try another wall socket
Inspect the cable for cuts, bends or burn marks
steps.resolves_if: A damaged cable: replace the charger

steps.step: Try a known-good charger of the same wattage
Inspect the laptop's charging port
steps.resolves_if: A loose port needs a technician

steps.step: Connect an external monitor
steps.expected: The external monitor shows a picture
steps.resolves_if: External works: the panel or its cable is at fault

steps.step: Raise the brightness and toggle the display shortcut (Fn key)
steps.resolves_if: It was set to minimum or off

steps.step: Update or roll back the graphics driver
steps.resolves_if: A driver change stops the flicker

steps.step: Open and close the lid slowly while watching the screen
steps.resolves_if: Flicker at some angles: the display cable needs a technician

steps.step: Replace the display panel
Test the keys in the BIOS setup screen or with an on-screen key tester
steps.resolves_if: Keys work in the BIOS: it is a software or driver problem

steps.step: Clean under the keys with compressed air
Reinstall the keyboard driver from Device Manager
Replace the keyboard
Use it on a hard, flat surface with the vents clear
Check Task Manager for a process using high CPU
steps.resolves_if: Closing a runaway process fixes it

steps.step: Update the BIOS and power-management drivers
Clean the vents and fan with compressed air
Replace the fan
Hard reset: unplug, hold power for 30 seconds, then plug in and start
steps.expected: Power and keyboard lights come on

steps.step: Start with only the charger connected, no USB devices
steps.resolves_if: A connected device was blocking start-up

steps.step: Check whether the BIOS setup screen opens (F2 at start-up)
steps.resolves_if: The BIOS opens: the operating system or the drive is at fault

steps.step: Reset the BIOS to defaults and replace the CMOS battery if the clock keeps resetting
steps.resolves_if: A CMOS battery replacement fixes it

steps.step: Run the drive self-test from the BIOS
steps.resolves_if: A failed drive needs an SSD replacement

title: Blue screen (BSOD) or corrupted operating system

steps.step: Note the stop code shown on the blue screen
steps.expected: A stop code such as CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED
steps.resolves_if: The code points to a known driver to fix

steps.step: Start in safe mode and uninstall the latest update or driver
Run sfc /scannow and DISM /RestoreHealth
Run the drive self-test
steps.resolves_if: A failed drive needs an SSD replacement

steps.step: Reinstall the operating system
Check free disk space (keep at least 15% free)
Disable unneeded start-up apps in Task Manager
Run a malware scan
Check the drive's health (SMART status)
steps.resolves_if: A failing drive needs an SSD replacement

steps.step: Check memory use under normal work
steps.resolves_if: Always above 80%: a RAM upgrade helps

steps.step: Forget the network and connect again
Turn off power saving for the Wi-Fi adapter in Device Manager
Update the Wi-Fi driver
Test on another network or a phone hotspot
steps.resolves_if: Stable elsewhere: the router is the problem

title: Touchpad or device stopped working after an update

steps.step: Check the touchpad isn't turned off (Fn shortcut or Settings)
Roll back the driver in Device Manager
Install the latest driver from the support site
Check the output device and volume in sound settings
steps.expected: The speakers are selected and unmuted

steps.step: Test with headphones
steps.resolves_if: Clear in headphones: the speakers need a technician

steps.step: Reinstall the audio driver
Check the power cable and the PSU switch at the back
steps.resolves_if: It was switched off or unplugged

steps.step: Disconnect every USB device and try again
Reset the BIOS by removing the CMOS battery for a minute
steps.expected: It starts and keeps the clock
steps.resolves_if: The clock keeps resetting: replace the CMOS battery

steps.step: Reseat the RAM sticks
Check the drive's health (SMART status)
steps.resolves_if: A failing drive needs an SSD replacement

steps.step: Check free disk space and start-up apps
steps.expected: At least 15% free, few start-up apps

steps.step: Check memory use under normal work
steps.resolves_if: Always above 80%: a RAM upgrade helps

steps.step: Clean the case fans and check temperatures
steps.resolves_if: A failed case fan needs replacing

steps.step: Check the balance slider in the phone or PC sound settings
Test with another phone or PC
steps.resolves_if: Both play: the first device is the problem

steps.step: Factory-reset the headphones (hold power and volume down for 10 seconds)
steps.expected: Both earcups play after pairing again

steps.step: Update the firmware from the Pulse app
Inspect the ear cushion and driver grille for damage
steps.resolves_if: Torn cushions: an ear cushion replacement

steps.step: Forget the headphones on the phone and pair again
Keep the phone within 5 metres with no walls between
Turn off multipoint in the Pulse app
steps.resolves_if: A second device was taking the connection

steps.step: Update the firmware from the Pulse app
Try another USB-C cable and a 5V wall adapter
steps.resolves_if: It charges with the other cable

steps.step: Clean the USB-C port gently with a dry brush
Leave it charging for 30 minutes before trying to turn it on
steps.resolves_if: A fully drained battery needed time
